result.title: Ambiguous Fits: The Rashomon Effect and Challenges in Scaling Law Estimation
result.summary: Estimating neural scaling laws involves an end-to-end pipeline: designing a scaling recipe, training models across scales, evaluating models on a target metric, and deploying an algorithm to fit a scaling law to the resulting data. This final fitting stage is often treated as routine: standard procedures minimize a non-convex fitting loss using local optimization from a grid of initializations, and return the best solution found. Yet such heuristic searches can fail in two distinct ways: they offer no guarantee of returning a nearly optimal solution, and they obscure whether fundamentally different parameter choices fit the data nearly as well. Indeed, we show that standard scaling law fitting is subject to a Rashomon effect (Breiman, 2001): the sublevel sets of near-minimizers correspond to broad parameter regions whose extrapolations diverge substantially at scale. We resolve these issues with a deterministic branch-and-bound algorithm that guarantees nearly optimal fitting loss and exhaustively maps the near-minimizers to the implied range of scaling curves.

AI.brief_summary: 指出常规 scaling law 拟合存在 Rashomon 效应：近最优参数区域很广，但外推曲线差异巨大；提出确定性的 branch-and-bound 算法，保证近最优拟合损失并穷举刻画近最优解对应的外推区间。
AI.relevance_reason: LVR 中常用 scaling law 论证 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的计算分配与长度泛化趋势，该文的可供核查线索是：把拟合不确定性显式映射为外推区间，可能帮助判断 latent 推理收益预测是否稳健。
